answer.evidence: The image is a full-width tile (160 px at every row) with two regions. Rows 0-31 are a dark brown rock wall, drawn face-on with a dark shadow strip at rows 29-31. Rows 32-143 are a flat ice floor seen from above (light blue, with a lighter edge at rows 32-34). The wall has no top surface, no front-edge line, no roof slope and no ellipse: it is only a vertical face. The floor is a large horizontal plane with no front face or front edge of its own. It is a room interior (back wall plus floor), not a standing building, gate or pavilion with a roof or lintel, so the structure kind does not fit well.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a flat room interior (a dark rock band on top and an ice floor), not a building with roof, walls and door or windows, so it does not match the reference kind. Measured facts: 7 colours per tile against 18 and 11 for the references, 52 distinct colours against 185 and 66, and 18% flat-fill coverage against 0% for both references. 92% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline leans near-black and has no material tint. The ice floor has some speckle, crack lines and pale patches, but only about 4 light-blue steps. The rock band is dark and has several brown steps, but it is small. Overall it is flatter and shallower than the references, with large smooth ice areas and neutral dark edges.
